work.title: The Red Book
work.creator: Carl Jung
work.practice: illuminated manuscript composition with layered visionary and exegetical registers

principle: Private timestamped experience is converted into doctrine by re-inscribing it with a later interpretive stratum inside a facsimile of an authority-conferring scriptural form while leaving every seam of that conversion visibly exposed.

nodes.label: Two-register stratification with dated anchoring
nodes.description: Each chapter pairs a dated first-person visionary episode transcribed from journals with a retrospective sermonic commentary in a distinct rhetorical register, held adjacent on the same page.
evidence: Documented in every chapter across all three books; strongest evidence density in the corpus per the validation stage.
Registers are typographically and rhetorically distinct: narrative past tense versus hortatory second-person address.
Commentary was composed months to years after the vision, placing two temporal positions in permanent adjacency on one page.
rules: Vision stratum and commentary stratum remain typographically and rhetorically distinguishable on the page
Each visionary episode carries a specific journal date

nodes.label: Codex facsimile plus archaizing diction
nodes.description: A hand-executed medieval manuscript system of Gothic textura script, rubrication, illumination, and gold leaf, unified with sustained biblical and Zarathustran syntax, apostrophe, and prophetic imperatives across hundreds of pages.
evidence: Governing constraint sustained across hundreds of pages and the entire material artifact per the validation stage.
Large folio bound in red leather, parchment then paper, with rubricated headings, historiated initials, ruled borders, and gold leaf.
Prose systematically imitates the Luther Bible and Zarathustra: inverted syntax, apostrophe, anaphoric repetition, prophetic imperatives.
rules: Medieval timelessness enforced across diction, script, codex, and pigment
The codex form claims finished, closed scripture

nodes.label: Dialogic episode construction
nodes.description: Content advances through direct dialogue with named figures such as Philemon, Elijah, and Salome, formatted as quasi-dramatic exchanges with alternating speakers and minimal narration.
evidence: Episodes proceed almost entirely through direct dialogue with named figures, following dramatic speech-attribution conventions.
Systematic across episodes but classified structurally subordinate to the stratification and facsimile mechanisms in the validation stage.

nodes.label: Element refusal in the Septem Sermones
nodes.description: One pseudonymous, doctrinal, non-narrative unit embedded within an otherwise experiential first-person system, violating the compression-to-extension alternation maintained everywhere else.
evidence: The seven sermons abandon narrative and dialogue for doctrinal aphoristic exposition attributed pseudonymously to Basilides of Alexandria.
Every other unit of the book is experiential and first-person; this unit is impersonal, catechistic, and third-voice.
The tensions stage argues the hierarchy reverses: hundreds of pages of pattern function as scaffolding for this one rupture.
rule_violations: First-person experiential narration as the default mode

nodes.label: Dated journal timestamps anchoring each episode
nodes.description: Episodes are pinned to specific nights, such as 12 November 1913 onward, imported from Black Books journal chronology; dates sequence the visions and expose the gap between experience and inscription.
evidence: Dates function as structural spine, not decoration, per the inventory.
Timestamps make the gap between vision and commentary measurable, converting double time into a verifiable structural fact.
rule_violations: Medieval timelessness enforced across diction, script, codex, and pigment

nodes.label: First-person visionary episode narratives
nodes.description: Dated first-person narrations of visionary episodes transcribed from the Black Books journals, typically one per titled chapter, compressed and dramatic in form.
evidence: Each chapter typically contains one visionary episode transcribed from the dated journals.
Episode length is short; commentary frequently doubles or triples it.

nodes.label: Retrospective sermonic commentary stratum
nodes.description: Elevated, hortatory commentary written months to years after each vision, in second-person address, materially co-present with the episode it interprets.
evidence: Commentary register is rhetorically distinct: hortatory second-person address versus narrative past tense.
Prophet and exegete are the same hand, nearly simultaneous; the commentary manufactures the scriptural authority it then dissects.

nodes.label: Archaizing biblical and Zarathustran diction
nodes.description: Sustained imitation of Luther Bible and Zarathustra registers: inverted syntax, apostrophe, anaphoric repetition, prophetic imperatives, maintained as a governing constraint across hundreds of pages.
evidence: Maintained across hundreds of pages as a governing constraint, not local ornament, per the inventory.

nodes.label: Medieval codex material system
nodes.description: Parchment and later paper, hand-drawn Gothic textura script, rubricated headings, illuminated initials, ruled borders, and gold leaf reproducing 13th to 15th century manuscript conventions.
evidence: The material system deliberately reproduces illuminated-manuscript conventions circa 13th to 15th century as compositional strategy.

nodes.label: Named interlocutor figures
nodes.description: Recurring named speakers including Elijah, Salome, the Red One, Ammonius, Izdubar, Philemon, the soul, and the dead, who carry the dialogic exchanges.
evidence: Episodes proceed almost entirely through direct dialogue with these named figures under dramatic speech-attribution conventions.

nodes.label: Compression-to-extension alternation rhythm
nodes.description: Regular oscillation between compressed dramatic episode and extended discursive elaboration, maintained without exception for hundreds of pages until the Septem Sermones.
evidence: Rhythm is generated by the oscillation of short episode followed by commentary that doubles or triples its length.
Predictability is manufactured precisely to make one violation legible, per the relationships stage.

nodes.label: Exposed production stratigraphy
nodes.description: The visible transmission chain from Black Books to Draft to Corrected Draft to calligraphic transcription, including revisions, the parchment-to-paper shift, and scribal hand variation across 1915 to circa 1930.
evidence: The scaffolding of manufacture is not concealed: draft layers, script variation, and the material shift remain visible in the artifact.
The years-long transcription produces the image-text proximity gradient, per the relationships stage.

nodes.label: Progressively decoupled painted image track
nodes.description: Full-page tempera and gouache paintings, including the mandala series, that begin tightly coupled to adjacent text and progressively drift until they occupy full pages with no textual referent.
evidence: Early sections keep image and text tightly coupled; later sections space them apart until paintings run referent-free.
Classified as a consequence of transcription duration rather than a designed constraint in the validation stage.
rules: Early sections establish tight image-text coupling before the drift begins

nodes.label: Terminal mid-sentence incompletion and unfinished epilogue
nodes.description: The calligraphic volume breaks off mid-sentence; a 1959 epilogue, itself unfinished, closes the artifact as an exposed, unrepaired edge.
evidence: Classified as structurally resonant but accidental, a boundary condition rather than an applied technique.
Denial is doubled: the codex withholds the closure its form promises, then the epilogue attempting repair also breaks off.

edges.rationale: The double-time effect requires diary timestamps; removing the dates collapses the two registers toward a single authorial voice.
The stratification pairs a dated visionary episode with commentary; without the episode stratum there is nothing for the commentary register to interpret.
Remove the commentary and the dates become mere journal apparatus; the call-and-response structure collapses into raw journal.
The medieval disguise depends structurally on the modern timestamps that betray it; subtracting the dates degrades the anachronism into mere pastiche.
Diary timestamps are irreducibly modern apparatus and no scripture carries them; they violate the medieval timelessness that every other element enforces, a productive rather than fatal tension.
The Sermones rupture requires the alternation rule to be maintained without exception; any prior violation would render the break illegible.
The unified scriptural frame needs its verbal half; the mechanism is defined as material and verbal medievalism operating as one system.
The unified scriptural frame needs its material half; the hand-executed manuscript system is the physical carrier of the disguise.
The archaizing diction requires the codex facsimile; biblical syntax alone would read as pastiche rather than governing system.
The codex facsimile requires the archaizing diction; Gothic textura alone would read as antiquarian craft rather than governing system.

Dialogic authority requires the scriptural frame; without the material-verbal medievalism the named figures speak without doctrinal weight. Philemon and Elijah carry authority because the frame is already established.
Remove the dialogic construction and the figures cease to exist as speakers; the mechanism is defined by their alternating exchanges.

As transcription duration extends past composition, image-text coupling degrades, driving paintings from illustration toward an independent track; the stratigraphy produces the proximity drift, not merely coexists with it.
The finished-scripture claim of the codex form is limited by exposed production stratigraphy, which continuously reveals the artifact as unclosed process; this contradiction is the content.
Commentary manufactures the authority of the prior text it interprets; if the commentary stratum increases in autonomy, the vision stratum loses its certified significance.
The compression-to-extension oscillation is generated by the episode-then-commentary pairing; without the two-register stratification there is no alternation to maintain or violate.
The codex form promises the closure of a completed sacred text; the mid-sentence break and unfinished 1959 epilogue refuse it, denying the ending and then denying the repair of that denial.
The exposed, unrepaired edge extends the same self-similar principle the stratigraphy displays: transmission is always incomplete and the incompletion is exposed rather than repaired.

violated: Vision stratum and commentary stratum remain typographically and rhetorically distinguishable on the page

failure_modes.consequence: If the reader collapses the strata, the work registers as either uniform scripture or uniform pastiche, and the dual perception of authority and fabrication fails.

Without the dated anchoring, the retrospective commentary becomes indistinguishable from the visions and the system flattens into one undifferentiated voice; the medieval disguise simultaneously degrades into mere pastiche.
If the alternation rule were violated more than once, the Sermones rupture would lose its singular structural force and read as inconsistency rather than designed break.

Concealing the production stratigraphy would let the facsimile succeed as forgery, eliminating the productive contradiction between finished form and ongoing process; the image-track drift would also lose its documented cause.

violated: Early sections establish tight image-text coupling before the drift begins

failure_modes.consequence: Fully decoupled images without the earlier tight coupling would present as arbitrary insertion rather than a measurable proximity drift across the codex.
Removing the two-register stratification collapses the book into either raw journal or standalone sermon; the dates become mere apparatus and the deepest load-bearing stratum is gone.

asserted_removal_tests.M1: If removed, the book collapses into either raw journal or standalone sermon; the measurable gap between vision-night and interpretation-moment disappears and the double-time structure breaks.
asserted_removal_tests.M2: If either half is removed, the other reads as pastiche or antiquarian craft; the scriptural frame collapses and the dialogic figures lose their doctrinal authority.
asserted_removal_tests.M3: If removed, the visionary content loses its dramatic engine, the figures cease to exist as speakers, and episodes become generic monologic description.
asserted_removal_tests.M4: If removed, the alternation rule loses the single rupture it was built to make legible, and the system's manufactured predictability serves no structural payoff.
